sonnet.problem: Card 1 says the man brings Ezekiel back to 'the gate that faces east.' Card 2 then asks which direction the glory is coming from. The setup already points to 'east' and lets the baker rule out north and south without reasoning about anything new.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for 'glory' in 'the ___ of the LORD fills the temple.' Cards 2, 3 and 6 already say 'the glory of the God of Israel,' 'His glory' and 'the glory of the LORD enters the temple.' The word is given away, so the question tests nothing, and 'smoke' and 'fire' are easy to dismiss.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. Once a choice has been answered, the cards after it can build on that answer. An easy follow-up is fine. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.
